_readme: Data for the Visual codes page. To add a code: add an object to the right category's 'codes' array. 'before'/'after' point to a webp pair in images/ (same subject, 4:3). Every webp must exist in TWO widths: name.webp (1168w) and name-584w.webp — the page builds srcset from that naming. Leave before/after out while the pair is not generated yet; the page then shows placeholder images automatically.

categories.title: See inside
categories.intro: Open up the subject and show what the eye cannot see — the classic teaching move.

codes.description: Opens the outer shell so students can look straight into the machine, building or vehicle.
Turns the photo into an X-ray view that reveals what hides under the surface.
Slices the subject cleanly through the middle, like a diagram in a textbook.
Pulls the parts apart in mid-air so every component and its place become visible.
Separates the subject into stacked layers — ideal for anything built up in strata.
Labels the body systems and structures of an animal or person, straight on the photo.
codes.addition: show the internal organs and skeleton beneath the skin, not just external body parts

codes.description: Shows the bones or supporting framework beneath the subject.
Reveals the components concealed behind a smooth, closed surface.
codes.addition: make the outer steel shell transparent so the concealed inner chamber, the double wall and the vacuum gap between them become visible

codes.description: Lets the hidden structure show through as faint outlines, leaving the outside intact.
codes.addition: make the walls and roof semi-transparent so the rooms, floors and timber frame inside show through as faint outlines

categories.title: Zoom to science scales
categories.intro: Bridge the visible world and the scales students can only imagine.

codes.description: Zooms from the photo down to cell level — a bridge from the visible to the microscopic.
Goes one step further and shows the subject at molecular scale.
Repaints the scene the way a heat camera sees it — great for energy and physics lessons.
Draws the invisible magnetic field lines around the subject.

categories.title: How things work
categories.intro: Turn any photo into a functional explanation of what is really going on.

codes.description: The all-round explainer: turns the photo into a visual walkthrough of how the thing works.
Zooms in on the gears, springs and levers that make the subject work.
Traces how power moves through the subject, from source to output.
Shows how air, water, blood or data streams through the subject.
codes.addition: show how blood flows through the body

codes.description: Visualises the forces at play — pressure, weight, lift, stress.
Draws the path a moving part, or the whole subject, follows.
Shows what enters the system and what comes out the other end.
codes.addition: show what goes into the tree and what comes out during photosynthesis

categories.title: Processes and time
categories.intro: Stretch a single moment into a sequence, a history or a whole life.

codes.description: Expands the photo into a full life cycle, from beginning to end.
Places the subject on a timeline and shows how it developed.
Compresses a slow process into a single image.
Breaks a task into numbered frames, step by step.
Shows the change — what it looked like, and what it became.
Shows how the separate parts go together, in numbered stages.

categories.title: Compare and decide
categories.intro: Put things side by side and let students reason about the difference.

codes.description: Puts the subject next to a hand or a person so its real size lands.
Lines up two versions in matching views so differences jump out.
codes.addition: compare it with a mobile phone from 2005 and label this one 2026

codes.description: Turns the subject into a clear advantages-and-drawbacks visual.
Maps the choices: what to do next at every branch.
codes.addition: draw a branching yes/no flowchart for sorting each item into the right recycling bin

categories.title: Technical drawing and math
categories.intro: Give any object the engineer's treatment — lines, grids, measurements and perspective.

codes.description: Redraws the photo as a classic technical blueprint.
Reduces the subject to a clean functional diagram.
codes.addition: redraw it as a technical circuit diagram with standard symbols for the battery, switch and lamp

codes.description: Shows accurate front, side and top views, like an engineer's sheet.
Adds measurements around the subject — instant math material.
Lays a grid over the subject for talking about size and proportion.
Exposes the perspective lines — a gift for art class.
Translates height and depth into contour lines, like a map.
Presents the subject as a CAD model, the way an engineer would draw it.
Identifies which material each part is made of.
codes.addition: colour-code every region by the material it is made of — steel, aluminium, rubber, leather, plastic — with a colour key, not by part name

categories.title: Classroom-ready annotations
categories.intro: Keep the photo, add the teaching layer on top.

codes.description: Keeps the photo intact and adds clean labels right on it.
Redraws the image as a hand-drawn whiteboard explanation.
Turns the photo into a poster with facts and labels.
Converts the subject into a data-rich infographic.
Condenses the task into a compact visual instruction card.
Shows the safety equipment the situation calls for.

categories.title: Body, life and environment
categories.intro: Turn a photo of a body, an animal or a place into biology teaching material.

codes.description: Labels the major muscles and shows where they sit.
Labels the internal organs — the dissection diagram without the dissection.
Shows how far a joint can move, and in which directions.
Moves the animal into the environment it actually lives in.
Maps how the species in a place depend on one another.
codes.addition: draw the food web showing which animals and plants in this pond depend on each other, with arrows for who eats whom
